notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after eleven searches (the five legislative candidates, the Mankato mayor's race and the two county attorneys), so everything else was read directly, one page at a time, with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py) and each site's robots.txt obeyed: the candidates' own sites, each county's, city's and school district's own pages, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates, the Scott County Republicans' site, and two news stories. A voter guide (theballotbrief.com) was read for leads only: it gave the address of Aaron Paul's campaign site, which was then opened and read.

Campaign websites already filed with the Secretary of State (read from sl_websites in the real database, opened read-only) were each opened before being listed. Xp Lee's filed site (https://xpleeformnhouse.com) answered 429 Too Many Requests three times and was not read, so it is not listed here; the filed address stands in our record.

Not read, and nothing worked around: Cook County's and the City of Mankato's sites and the Minnesota Judicial Branch's directory (robots.txt disallows our reader), Nobles County's site (an empty page without scripts), Bemidji Area Schools (a TLS handshake failure; certificate checking was not turned off), the Secretary of State's appointments site (never requested). So Debra K. White, Chris Dybevick, Dave Wall and Elizabeth H. Strand have no findings.

Looked for on the government's own page and not there as a sitting member (so nothing is recorded): Adam A. Gast (Marshall County's sheriff page names another sheriff), Dolly Wussow (Brainerd council), Lee Albert Wickboldt (Hastings council), Travis Sundberg (Oakdale council), Liz Magill (Red Wing council), Mel Joseph (Lakeville board; the district's election page lists Mel Joseph as a filed candidate, nothing more), Jason Spry (Delano board page), Jon Beulke (New Prague). Nick Gleason (Waconia) and Dakota S Helmbrecht (Mora): the council and board pages could not be found without a search.

For the second reader: (1) 'elected 2010' and 'elected 2018' are written in 'from' where the page gives an election year and not the year a term began, as in part 16. (2) Itasca County writes 'John Johnson' and Martin County 'Richard Koons' without the middle name our list carries; each is tied to the race by the county and the district seat sought, whose term the page says ends in 2026, but John Johnson is a common name: if the District 3 race has a challenger of the same name, the county's page cannot tell them apart. (3) Jason Baskin's port authority, human rights commission and housing authority posts are city public bodies named on the city's own page, without years; his seats on private boards on the same page were left out. (4) Aaron Paul's own Endorsements page is headed 'Previous Endorsements and Distinctions - 2024' and says the Scott County GOP endorsed him on May 8th, 2024; that is about 2024, so it is not recorded as an endorsement or as his own words for 2026. The Scott County Republicans' 'Endorsed/Recommended Candidates' page shows no names as text. No Republican party page with a 2026 endorsement of Aaron Paul or Scott Van Binsbergen was found, and no campaign site for Van Binsbergen. (5) Julia Hamann's Endorsements page also thanks the Blue Earth County DFL for a 'letter of support' and says the DFL cannot endorse for the nonpartisan office; it is on her site, not the party's, so it is not an endorsed_by. (6) Simon Glaser's Endorsements page shows its endorsers as images, so no own_words for him. (7) Scott Dibble's own_words carries a 'where' key (which the loader does not read) because the quoted words are a list entry under a heading. (8) endorsed_by entries carry 'listed_as', the line on the DFL's page. (9) Read and left out on purpose for everyone: jobs and employers, schools, family and household, faith, and seats on private boards and associations.
